flashcards.q: What does a topological sort guarantee about every edge u->v?
flashcards.a: u appears before v in the resulting linear order. Only possible when the graph is a DAG (no cycle).

flashcards.q: Describe Kahn's algorithm in one sentence.
flashcards.a: Repeatedly remove nodes with in-degree 0, appending them to the order and decrementing their neighbors' in-degree, until the queue empties.

flashcards.q: How does Kahn's algorithm detect a cycle for free?
flashcards.a: If the final processed-node count is less than the total node count, the unprocessed nodes are part of one or more cycles.

flashcards.q: Why does DFS-based topological sort need three colors instead of a simple visited/unvisited boolean?
flashcards.a: A GRAY (in-progress, still on the recursion stack) revisit is a real back-edge/cycle; a BLACK (already fully processed) revisit is just a forward/cross edge, not a cycle. Two states can't distinguish them.

flashcards.q: Why must you reverse DFS postorder to get a valid topological order?
flashcards.a: Postorder finalizes a node only after everything reachable from it, so dependents get pushed before their prerequisites; reversing restores prerequisite-first order.

flashcards.q: What is the time and space complexity of topological sort (either method)?
flashcards.a: O(V+E) time and O(V+E) space for both Kahn's and DFS-based implementations.

flashcards.q: How do you find the minimum number of 'rounds' to complete all tasks when independent tasks can run in parallel (Parallel Courses, LC 1136)?
flashcards.a: Run Kahn's algorithm processing one full in-degree-zero frontier per round instead of one node at a time; count rounds until the queue empties.

flashcards.q: For Alien Dictionary, where do the graph edges come from?
flashcards.a: Compare each pair of adjacent sorted words, find the first differing character, and add a directed edge from the earlier alphabet character to the later one.
